newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait sells 30mln Real Estate Bank shares.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait sells 30mln Real Estate Bank shares.

text.p: Kuwait has sold 30 percent of its 100 million shares in Kuwait Real Estate Bank (KREB) in a public auction for 12.55 million dinars ($41.97 million), local dailies said on Friday.
It was the first step of a privatisation plan, they added.
The Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA), the state investment arm, on Thursday sold 20 million KREB shares at the starting price of 410 fils ($1.37) to the Securities Group, they added.
Another 10 million shares were sold at 435 fils to a private investor, they said. KREB share closed on Wednesday at 425 fils.
KIA has said it plans to sell another 60 million shares in a public subscription at a later stage. The price for the subscription is yet to be announced.
Kuwait has a 32.9 percent stake in KREB, which mainly extends medium and long-term loans to construction and commercial projects and property investment.
The bank reported a 101.8 percent rise in net profit in the first half of 1996 compared with the same period last year, rising to 3.5 million dinars.

The sale is part of Kuwait's plan to shed state holdings in about 60 local firms and public services such as electricity, water and telecommunications. The plan, announced after the 1991 Gulf War, is supervised by KIA.
